vocabulary.meaning_en: not healthy; having an illness
vocabulary.note_ar: sick و ill بنفس المعنى تقريباً؛ sick أشيع في الكلام الأمريكي.
vocabulary.note_en: sick and ill mean almost the same; sick is more common in American speech.
vocabulary.example: I can't go to school today. I'm sick.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to go to your workplace
vocabulary.note_en: Used when you talk to your boss: "I can't come in today."
vocabulary.example: I can't come in today. I have a fever.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the person who is in charge of you at work
vocabulary.example: My boss is very kind.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to put color on something with a brush
vocabulary.example: We painted the kitchen white.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to divide something with a knife or a tool
vocabulary.note_en: The past form is the same: cut → cut.
vocabulary.example: He cut the bread into four pieces.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the hard material that trees are made of
vocabulary.example: This table is made of wood.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to make something by putting parts together
vocabulary.example: They built a new school in our town.

vocabulary.meaning_en: flames and heat from something burning
vocabulary.note_ar: build a fire = يُشعل ناراً (يجمع الحطب ويشعله).
vocabulary.note_en: build a fire = make a fire with wood.
vocabulary.example: We sat near the fire to get warm.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to have a feeling in your body or mind
vocabulary.example: I felt tired after the long day.

vocabulary.meaning_en: healthy; not sick
vocabulary.note_en: Here "well" is an adjective meaning healthy.
vocabulary.example: I don't feel well today.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a common illness with fever, cough and pain
vocabulary.example: She had the flu last winter.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to rest with your eyes closed
vocabulary.example: I slept for ten hours last night.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to take water or another liquid into your mouth
vocabulary.example: He drank a big glass of water.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person whose job is to help sick people
vocabulary.example: You should see a doctor.

vocabulary.meaning_en: time when you relax or sleep and do no work
vocabulary.note_ar: get lots of rest = ارتح كثيراً.
vocabulary.note_en: get lots of rest = rest a lot.
vocabulary.example: After the trip, I need some rest.

vocabulary.meaning_en: pain in your throat
vocabulary.example: I have a sore throat, so I can't talk much.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a loud push of air from your throat when you are sick
vocabulary.example: He has a bad cough.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a body temperature that is higher than normal
vocabulary.example: The child has a fever.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a tool that measures temperature
vocabulary.example: Put the thermometer under your tongue.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a unit for measuring temperature
vocabulary.note_ar: في أمريكا تُقاس الحرارة بالفهرنهايت؛ 100.5 فهرنهايت ≈ 38 مئوية.
vocabulary.note_en: The US uses Fahrenheit: 100.5°F is about 38°C.
vocabulary.example: It is 30 degrees today.

vocabulary.meaning_en: above the normal level
vocabulary.example: His temperature is very high.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person you work with
vocabulary.example: My co-workers helped me with the project.

vocabulary.meaning_en: two, or a small number
vocabulary.example: I'll be back in a couple of days.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to cause pain or harm
vocabulary.note_en: "It can't hurt" = it will not do any harm.
vocabulary.example: My leg hurts.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to push air out of your nose suddenly and loudly
vocabulary.example: Dust makes me sneeze.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a film you watch
vocabulary.example: Let's watch a movie tonight.

fine_lines.title: sick vs ill
fine_lines.explanation_ar: كلاهما يعني «مريض». sick أشيع في الكلام اليومي الأمريكي ويأتي قبل الاسم (a sick child). ill أشيع في بريطانيا ويأتي غالباً بعد الفعل (He is ill).
fine_lines.explanation_en: Both mean not healthy. Sick is more common in everyday American English and can go before a noun (a sick child). Ill is more common in British English and usually comes after the verb (He is ill).

examples.sentence: I'm sick. I can't come to work.
She is taking care of her sick mother.
He was ill for a week.

fine_lines.title: feel well vs feel good
fine_lines.explanation_ar: feel well = أشعر أني بصحة جيدة (عن المرض). feel good = أشعر بالراحة أو السعادة، وقد تُستخدم للصحة أيضاً. في النفي عن المرض نقول عادة: I don't feel well.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Feel well" is about health: not sick. "Feel good" is about being happy or comfortable, and sometimes health too. To say you are sick, we often say "I don't feel well."

examples.sentence: I don't feel well. I think I have a cold.
I feel good after my morning walk.

fine_lines.title: flu vs fever
fine_lines.explanation_ar: flu اسم المرض (الإنفلونزا). fever عَرَض: ارتفاع حرارة الجسم. قد يسبّب الـ flu حُمّى fever.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Flu is an illness. A fever is a sign of illness: a high body temperature. The flu can give you a fever.

examples.sentence: I had the flu last week.

expressions.phrase: I can't come to work today.
expressions.meaning_ar: لا أستطيع الحضور إلى العمل اليوم.
expressions.meaning_en: I am not able to go to work today.
expressions.example: Hello, Ms. Lee. I can't come to work today. I'm sick.
You look tired. What is wrong?
I don't feel well. I want to go home.

expressions.meaning_en: A polite answer to bad news.
expressions.example: "My cat is sick." "I'm sorry to hear that."

expressions.meaning_en: Advice: it is a good idea to call your doctor.
expressions.example: You have a high fever. You should call your doctor.

expressions.meaning_en: Rest a lot so you get better.
expressions.example: Drink water and get lots of rest!

expressions.meaning_en: A polite question from someone who wants to help.
expressions.example: Good morning. How can I help you?

expressions.phrase: Do you have a sore throat?
expressions.meaning_en: A doctor's question about pain in the throat.
expressions.example: Do you have a sore throat or a cough?

expressions.phrase: When did you start feeling sick?
expressions.example: "When did you start feeling sick?" "Last night."

expressions.phrase: Call me back in a couple of days.
expressions.meaning_ar: اتصل بي مرة أخرى بعد يومين.
expressions.meaning_en: Phone me again after two or three days.
expressions.example: I'm busy now. Call me back in a couple of days.

expressions.meaning_en: It will not cause any problem, so you can try it.
expressions.example: Drink some hot tea. It can't hurt!

grammar.title: Simple past: irregular verbs
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم الماضي البسيط لحدث انتهى في الماضي (yesterday, last week). الأفعال المنتظمة تأخذ ed (paint → painted). لكن أفعالاً كثيرة شاذة ولها شكل خاص يجب حفظه: feel → felt، cut → cut، build → built، have → had، sleep → slept، drink → drank، hear → heard، say → said. الشكل نفسه مع كل الضمائر (I/you/he/she/we/they).
grammar.explanation_en: We use the simple past for actions that finished in the past (yesterday, last week). Regular verbs add -ed (paint → painted). Many verbs are irregular and have a special past form you must learn: feel → felt, cut → cut, build → built, have → had, sleep → slept, drink → drank, hear → heard, say → said. The form is the same for every subject.
examples: In the afternoon, I cut wood. Then I built a fire.
I had the flu last week.
I slept a lot and drank a lot of water.

grammar.title: Talking about illness: have + a/an + problem
grammar.explanation_ar: للحديث عن المرض نستخدم have: I have a cough / a fever / a sore throat / the flu. والسؤال: Do you have a fever? والإجابة: Yes, I do. / No, I don't. ومع he/she نقول has.
grammar.explanation_en: To talk about illness we use have: I have a cough / a fever / a sore throat / the flu. Question: Do you have a fever? Short answers: Yes, I do. / No, I don't. With he/she/it use has.
examples: Do you have a cough? - Yes, I do.

grammar.title: Should for advice
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم should + الفعل الأساسي لإعطاء نصيحة. لا نضيف to ولا s: You should call your doctor (وليس should to call / should calls). النفي: shouldn't.
grammar.explanation_en: Use should + base verb to give advice. Do not add "to" or -s: You should call your doctor. Negative: shouldn't.
examples: He should drink lots of water.
You shouldn't go to work today.

questions.question: What is the past form of "feel"?
questions.explanation_ar: الماضي الشاذ من feel هو felt.

questions.question: Caty was sick last week. She ___ the flu.
Which sentence gives correct advice?
questions.explanation_ar: بعد should يأتي الفعل الأساسي بدون to.
questions.explanation_en: After "should" we use the base verb without "to".

questions.question: "I have a sore throat" means:
questions.explanation_en: A sore throat is pain in your throat.

questions.question: "Don't go to work for a couple of days." A couple of days is about:
questions.explanation_ar: a couple of = اثنان أو عدد قليل.
questions.explanation_en: "A couple of" means two or a small number.

questions.question: Your friend says, "I'm sick." What is a polite answer?
questions.explanation_ar: نقول I'm sorry to hear that عند سماع خبر سيئ.
questions.explanation_en: We say "I'm sorry to hear that" when we hear bad news.

questions.question: I don't feel ___. I think I have the flu.
questions.explanation_ar: I don't feel well = لا أشعر أني بصحة جيدة.
questions.explanation_en: "I don't feel well" means I feel sick.
